findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] flusher.py (join) — When the deadline expires, the new `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the loop before calling `process.terminate()`, leaving remaining flusher child processes running when `join()` returns; orphaned spawn processes can keep producing to Kafka after shutdown (the old code always terminated the process after the wait loop)

[Medium/data] flusher.py (submit, memory check) — Summing `used`/`available` across all per-shard `SpansBuffer` instances distorts the `used / available` ratio when shards from different process groups share the same Redis host, potentially triggering spurious `MessageRejected` backpressure or missing real memory pressure; aggregation should deduplicate by Redis host instead of summing per-buffer values

[Medium/performance] flusher.py (main) — Metric tags now include `shard`/`shards` values like `"0,2"` on `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce`, and `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy`, creating high-cardinality tag combinations; the tag key is also inconsistent (`"shard"` in produce/segment_size_bytes/flusher_unhealthy vs `"shards"` in wait_produce), fragmenting dashboards/alerts

[Low/bug] flusher.py (__init__) — `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit `flusher_processes=0` as falsy and silently falls back to one process per shard, contradicting the CLI option; the `--flusher-processes` option also lacks `>= 1` validation

[Medium/test_gap] tests — No test covers the multi-process health/restart path (`_ensure_processes_alive`): crash detection, per-process `process_restarts` accounting, the `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`, or that a restarted process handles the correct shard subset; the `--flusher-processes` CLI wiring in `consumers/__init__.py` is also untested

[Low/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py:test_flusher_processes_limit — The test only asserts internal bookkeeping (`len(flusher.processes)`, shard mapping counts); `messages` is never checked, so it does not verify that flushing actually works with shard-to-process sharing

[Low/bug] flusher.py — `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code: nothing calls it. Either remove it or, if restart-per-shard was intended, it's unimplemented (restarts always replace the whole process group)

[Low/doc] flusher.py — The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard" but the code creates one process per group of shards; likewise the comment "Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy" sits on a purely process-level hang check and is misleading

[Low/bug] flusher.py (_ensure_processes_alive) — `metrics.incr(..., tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})` passes an `int` shard value as a tag; several metrics backends require string tag values and will fail or coerce inconsistently

[Medium/bug] flusher.py (_ensure_processes_alive) — The restart counter `process_restarts[process_index]` is incremented before checking whether the replacement process actually starts successfully and is never reset on recovery; a single slow-to-spawn process (spawn import time counts against `healthy_since`, set optimistically at creation) can burn through `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` and crash the consumer, and per-process sharding amplifies this since each unhealthy check restarts all shards in the group

[Low/bug] flusher.py (join) — For thread-based flushers (`produce_to_pipe` set), after the deadline passes the thread is neither terminated nor joined; a hung thread survives `join()` while its replacement thread may already have been started by `_ensure_processes_alive`, allowing two threads to produce duplicates concurrently

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] flusher.py (submit, memory check) — Summing `used`/`available` across all per-shard `SpansBuffer` instances distorts the `used / available` ratio when shards from different process groups share the same Redis host, potentially triggering spurious `MessageRejected` backpressure or missing real memory pressure; aggregation should deduplicate by Redis host instead of summing per-buffer values

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the memory-pressure check in `SpanFlusher.submit` from a single buffer (`memory_infos = list(self.buffer.get_memory_info())`) to aggregating across multiple per-process/per-shard buffers (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())` and then summing `used`/`available`). If multiple `SpansBuffer` instances report the same underlying Redis/service memory stats, this could double-count and skew `used / available`, affecting `MessageRejected` backpressure decisions. However, the diff does not show what `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` returns (e.g., per-redis-host vs per-shard), so the distortion is a plausible review concern created by the change but not strictly verifiable as a definite defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] flusher.py (__init__) — `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit `flusher_processes=0` as falsy and silently falls back to one process per shard, contradicting the CLI option; the `--flusher-processes` option also lacks `>= 1` validation

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will treat an explicit `max_processes=0` (coming from the new `--flusher-processes` click option) as falsy and replace it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, silently ignoring the user-provided value. The new click option (`click.Option(... type=int ...)`) adds no `min=1`/validation, so `0` is allowed by the diff as written, making this an observable incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests — No test covers the multi-process health/restart path (`_ensure_processes_alive`): crash detection, per-process `process_restarts` accounting, the `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`, or that a restarted process handles the correct shard subset; the `--flusher-processes` CLI wiring in `consumers/__init__.py` is also untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior in `SpanFlusher`: multi-process shard-to-process mapping (`process_to_shards_map`), per-process health/backpressure tracking (`process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`), restart accounting (`process_restarts`), and restart/kill logic in `_ensure_processes_alive` including raising `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`. The new/updated tests only cover (a) basic flow timing tweaks and (b) that `flusher_processes` limits the number of processes and shard distribution (`test_flusher_processes_limit`), plus backpressure assertion change. There is no test exercising the crash/hang detection branches, restart counter behavior, `RuntimeError` threshold, or verifying that after a restart the process is recreated for the same shard subset. Separately, the CLI wiring adds a new Click option `--flusher-processes` in `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py`, but no test in the diff asserts this option is present or correctly plumbed into `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory`/`SpanFlusher`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py:test_flusher_processes_limit — The test only asserts internal bookkeeping (`len(flusher.processes)`, shard mapping counts); `messages` is never checked, so it does not verify that flushing actually works with shard-to-process sharing

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` (in `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py`, not `test_flusher.py`) that asserts internal state only: `len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes/num_processes`, and shard distribution via `process_to_shards_map`. It never asserts any observable flushing behavior (e.g., that `messages` receives produced `KafkaPayload`s when shards share a process), so it doesn’t validate the new shard-to-process sharing logic beyond bookkeeping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] flusher.py — `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code: nothing calls it. Either remove it or, if restart-per-shard was intended, it's unimplemented (restarts always replace the whole process group)

adjudication.rationale: In flusher.py, `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is newly added but never referenced in the diff. Restarts are handled in `_ensure_processes_alive()` by calling `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` (i.e., per process group), with no call site that would restart a single shard via `_create_process_for_shard`. This is dead/unused code or indicates an unimplemented intended behavior, but it does not by itself constitute a verifiable correctness bug since it is not executed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc] flusher.py — The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard" but the code creates one process per group of shards; likewise the comment "Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy" sits on a purely process-level hang check and is misleading

adjudication.rationale: The diff updates SpanFlusher docstring to say "Creates one process per shard" (flusher.py), but the implementation explicitly groups shards into at most `num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` and assigns shards via modulo into `process_to_shards_map`, meaning one process may handle multiple shards. Also in `_ensure_processes_alive`, the hang condition is purely `time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds` (process-level), so the comment "Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy" is misleading given there is no per-shard health check there. This is a real documentation/comment accuracy issue, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] flusher.py (_ensure_processes_alive) — `metrics.incr(..., tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})` passes an `int` shard value as a tag; several metrics backends require string tag values and will fail or coerce inconsistently

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the diff adds `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})` where `shard` comes from `for shard in shards:` and is an `int` (partition/shard id). The diff does not show whether `sentry.utils.metrics` requires tag values to be strings or safely coerces non-strings, so a definite runtime failure cannot be verified from the PR alone. However, it is a concrete, diff-introduced concern because other tag usage in this file was changed to explicitly build a string tag (`shard_tag = ",".join(...)`) suggesting string tags are expected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] flusher.py (_ensure_processes_alive) — The restart counter `process_restarts[process_index]` is incremented before checking whether the replacement process actually starts successfully and is never reset on recovery; a single slow-to-spawn process (spawn import time counts against `healthy_since`, set optimistically at creation) can burn through `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` and crash the consumer, and per-process sharding amplifies this since each unhealthy check restarts all shards in the group

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, `process_healthy_since[process_index]` is set to `int(time.time())` *before* the new process/thread is started, and the actual `healthy_since` update only happens inside `main`’s loop. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, a process can be deemed unhealthy solely because `time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds` even if it’s merely slow to start (spawn/import time) and hasn’t reached the point where it updates `healthy_since` yet, causing repeated restarts. The restart counter `process_restarts[process_index]` is monotonically incremented on each such unhealthy detection and is never reset on recovery, so repeated false-positive “hang” detections can eventually exceed `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` and raise, crashing the consumer. (The finding’s sub-claim that it is incremented *before* checking the threshold is inaccurate; the diff shows the `> MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` check happens before the increment.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] flusher.py (join) — For thread-based flushers (`produce_to_pipe` set), after the deadline passes the thread is neither terminated nor joined; a hung thread survives `join()` while its replacement thread may already have been started by `_ensure_processes_alive`, allowing two threads to produce duplicates concurrently

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe` set), `_ensure_processes_alive` will restart an “unhealthy” flusher by calling `_create_process_for_shards(...)` without stopping the existing thread. The restart path only attempts `kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so a hung `threading.Thread` is never terminated, yet a new thread for the same `shards` is started and replaces the dict entry (`self.processes[process_index] = process`), losing the old reference. Separately, `join()` only busy-waits on the threads currently referenced in `self.processes` and does not `join()` threads; once the deadline is exceeded it stops waiting and does not/cannot terminate threads. Together this makes it possible for a hung old thread to survive while a replacement thread runs concurrently for the same shards, which can lead to concurrent flushing/producing for the same shards.
